newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Germany's Kinkel backs Slovenia UN bid.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kinkel backs Slovenia UN bid.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Tuesday Germany would support Slovenia's bid to become a non-permanent member of the United Nations Security Council.

"From our point of view Slovenia is definitely a country that fulfils all the necessary conditions for becoming a non-permanent member of the Security Council," Kinkel told a news conference after meeting Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek.
Slovenia has already announced its candidacy for Security Council membership from 1998 to 1999.

Kinkel, in Slovenia on a one-day visit, said Germany would also back Slovenia's bid to join the European Union and NATO. Slovenia hopes to become a full member of NATO as soon as possible and to join the EU by 2001.
Germany is Slovenia's most important trading partner and last year accounted for about 30 percent of Slovenia's exports and 23 percent of its imports.
